curated.instructions: omr/instructions/8218-1/ (scans; pages 3-12 the body and engine, 13-14 the front fork, 15-16 the fork joined on and the finished trike)

functions.does: Rolling the trike turns the right rear wheel, whose axle turns the crank under the engine and pumps the yellow piston up and down in the cylinder; the cylinder stays put on the frame.
functions.source: book: steps 3-4 (cylinder), 9-12 (axle, crank, connecting rod and piston, wheels; step 11 rings the crank)

functions.does: The left rear wheel turns freely on its own axle pin and doesn't drive the engine.
functions.source: book: steps 9 and 12 (an axle pin in the frame's end hole carries the left wheel; the axle that drives the crank comes in from the right)

functions.does: The front wheel rolls freely on its axle between the fork's tips.
The handlebars steer the front fork, which swivels on a single friction pin at the front of the frame, turning the front wheel left and right.
functions.source: book: front fork steps 1-7, steps 15-16 (the fork's cross block is pushed onto the friction pin); inferred: that the fork swivels, since one pin is all that holds it, and the book draws no arrow
functions.note: the pin is a friction pin, so the fork turns stiffly and stays where it's left
